newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to meet U.S. envoy to talk peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to meet U.S. envoy to talk peace.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross will meet on Friday night with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in a last effort to revive Israeli-PLO peace talks before heading home, a Palestinian official said.
"President Arafat will meet Dennis Ross at 830 p.m. (1730 GMT) in Nablus before the American envoy leaves the region," said Nabil Abu Rdainah, Arafat's adviser.
Arafat declined to meet Ross on Thursday.
Another PLO official said Ross asked to meet Arafat during talks on Friday with top Palestinian negotiators Saeb Erekat and Mahmoud Abbas.
"Arafat will meet Ross although he is not happy with the American mediation role and the results of the Israeli-Palestinian talks that were held in Tel Aviv earlier this week," Abu Rdainah said.
Ross met earlier on Friday with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.

"The prime minister (Benjamin Netanyahu) delivered a report to the ministers that there is no real progress in the contacts between us and the Palestinian Authority," the government said in a statement after its weekly meeting on Friday.
Palestinian officials agreed with Israel's assessment.
"Ross's mission has failed completely," Marwan Kanafani, a spokesman for Arafat, told Reuters.

The American envoy doggedly shuttled between the sides but failed to budge them from positions hardened during a two-month freeze sparked by Israel's groundbreaking of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Palestinians demand Israel halt all settlement activity as a precondition to resuming talks. Israel has refused and called on the Palestinians to do more to fight "terror".
